Subject: Hosted API billing setup and invoice options

Hi Vanessa,

We're getting close to ramping usage against Redwood's Hosted API and I need to line up our finance/billing setup. A few quick questions:

- Can Acme be invoiced monthly (Net-30) instead of charging a corporate card?
- Do you support ACH payments and is there a preferred remit-to address?
- What documentation do you need for Net terms (W-9, PO, credit references)?
- Are there committed-spend discounts or standard tier breaks we should consider? We expect ~$45k/month initially across three internal teams.

I've attached a PO template for reference (Acme_PO_20260914.pdf). Please let me know the fastest path to start on monthly invoicing if possible.

Thanks,
Samantha Wu
Head of Procurement
Acme Analytics

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 19:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API billing setup and invoice options

Hi Samantha — thanks for the note and for sharing the PO. Short answers up front: yes, we support monthly invoicing (Net-30) and ACH/wire; there is a short review process. Below are the details and next steps to move you from card-on-file to invoice billing.

1) Eligibility & timeline
- Eligibility: accounts with recurring spend typically > $10k/mo are eligible for Net-30 after Finance review. Your $45k/mo looks fine for that path.
- Timeline: 3–7 business days after we receive the signed billing agreement + W-9 + PO.

2) Required docs
- W-9 (US customers) or W-8 (non-US)
- Signed billing terms / Net Terms Request Form (attached: NetTermsRequestForm.pdf)
- PO (you already attached one)
- Bank remit details (for ACH) or wire instructions if you prefer wire payments

3) Operational notes
- We issue consolidated monthly invoices and can roll up charges across multiple internal teams under a single billing account.
- Default payment terms: Net-30 with a card fallback until the first invoice clears for new customers. For larger committed contracts we can waive the card fallback.

4) Discounts & commitments
- We have standard committed-discount tiers handled by Sales Ops; typical discounts require a 6–12 month revenue commit and are applied to a committed monthly/annual spend.
- If you can share a committed monthly amount (or annual target) we can run a quick pricing model and propose a tier.

Next steps: please send a billing contact, the PO number to reference, and the signed NetTermsRequestForm. I’ll loop in Finance (Ben) and Accounts (Lauren) to start the review. If you prefer, we can do a 30-minute billing setup call later this week.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0147

Hi Samantha — Ben from Finance here. Thanks Vanessa — a couple of clarifications from our side to speed the onboarding:

- Underwriting: we do a basic credit check and verify PO + W-9. For first-time Net-30 customers we'll typically ask for one of: (a) two vendor references, (b) a short-term retainer/prepay equal to one invoice cycle, or (c) a corporate guarantor. Because your expected run-rate is >$40k/mo we can be flexible.
- Payment rails: ACH is preferred; for wire remittance we will provide bank details on the invoice. Please provide the exact remit-to address and the Acme EFT/ACH details when available.
- Card fallback: if an invoice ages beyond 45 days we reserve the right to temporarily suspend billing privileges until resolved — this is rare but we'd like you to be aware.

If you plan to ask for a committed-spend discount we typically require a written commitment (term + committed monthly/annual $) before giving a list-price reduction. Send the proposed commitment and I’ll run numbers with Accounting.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
